newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DG Bank buys 55.98pct stake in Hungary Takarekbank.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank buys 55.98pct stake in Hungary Takarekbank.

text.p: Germany's DG Bank on Friday signed a contract for the purchase from the Hungarian government of a 55.98 percent stake in Takarekbank, the umbrella bank of Hungary's savings cooperatives.
Hungaria Biztosito, the Hungarian insurance arm of Germany's Allianz AG also bought a five percent stake.
The total 60.98 percent stake has a face value of 817.6 million forints ($4.35 million), and it was sold at 532 percent of face value.
DG Bank said in a statement that it would increase Takarekbank's capital by 350 million forints, buying new shares at 200 percent of face value.
It added that it also planned to invest 20 million German marks in information technology developments in the Hungarian savings cooperatives sector.

Friedbert Malt, member of DG Bank's board of directors, told a news conference following the signing of the privatisation contract that DG Bank, which has a similar role in Germany as Takarekbank, plans to introduce high standard banking services in Hungary's savings cooperative sector.

"We do not expect Hungarian sevings cooperatives to reach the 20 percent market share (of their German counterparts) from one day to the other," he said. "But we are working on increasing their market share from the current five percent to 10 percent."

The savings cooperatives grouping around Takarekbank make up Hungary's largest banking network, with 1600 units, most of them located to small towns and villages where they have hardly any competition locally.

Takarekbank CEO Zsolt Hernadi said the bank boosted its balance sheet total to 85 billion forints by the end of May from 66.5 billion at the end of 1996, while its pre-tax profit was 597 million forints, almost equal to the 623 million forints posted in the whole of 1996.
He added that the group of the savings cooperatives produced similar growth figures.
